packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, one packet per session, prompt and images only (reader brief of PR #76/#77); repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; reread of packets whose first readings were written after the session's image limit had removed earlier images
text:
packet-18 -- blind image reading (unverified)
Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this record. The parent brief path names a collection batch ("stams-c5ugo") and the shelf labels on the strips read "Stams, StA, Frg. 254-1r / 254-2r / 254-1v / 254-2v" (pencil, modern); I did not use these for anything beyond face labelling.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overviews image-001 and image-010)
- image-001: two narrow vertical parchment strips (binding strips, c. 4-5 cm wide, c. 50 cm long), photographed side by side, colour card upper left, scale bottom. Pencil labels at top: left strip "Stams, StA, Frg. 254-2r"(?), right strip "Stams, StA, Frg. 254-1r"(?).
  * Left strip: text begins about one third down (above it blank/stained parchment with holes). One column fragment, lines cut on both sides (only a few letters per line, roughly 6-10 letters visible). Blue and red alternating 2-line initials at the right edge of the text area (P blue, I red, P blue, then smaller blue/red paragraph-type initials lower down). Small marginal letters ("b") to the right. Small textura, many lines.
  * Right strip: text along the whole length, also cut letters-wide. Upper part: one narrow column with marginal notes in a smaller hand to the right; alternating red/blue initials (P, P, P, P ... , R/P blue-red, later blue O/e). Lower third: a ruled frame (red/blue penwork border lines) enclosing text, with red marginal marks; at the bottom a red/blue rubric line "...l. expansion. nou..."(?) and a large initial "Q"/"O" in red/blue.
- image-010 (the other face): same two strips reversed. Text very faint/abraded. Left strip has at top a penwork border fragment, faint text in upper part, and a few lines of later cursive marginal notes around mid-length and lower; faint traces of coloured initials. Right strip has a block of dense small cursive (later?) text in its upper part, faint initials (blue "P", green-ish "D"?) further down, mostly blank/abraded.
Tentative interpretation: strips cut from a two-column(?) glossed or legal/scholastic book in textura, with alternating red/blue initials marking short paragraphs; reused in a binding. Column width cannot be established; only fragments of each line survive.
Tile plan (assumed): image-002..009 = native tiles of face image-001 (2 across x 4 down); image-011..018 = native tiles of face image-010.

=== image-002 (face image-001, LEFT strip "Frg. 254-2r", top section) ===
Mostly blank stained parchment with worm/rodent holes; pencil shelfmark "Stams, StA / Frg. 254-2r". Text begins only at the very bottom of the tile (cut off; these lines recur at top of the next tile below, so read there). Visible at bottom: line with a red initial-like stroke at right edge "...[a]nifest(?)" and above it two lines starting "c(on)..."; a very faint marginal note at right ("...ypo(?) / ...ame"?) illegible.
Note: the strip's text is upside down relative to the label? No - text appears right way up but the letters shown are truncated at left; only the right-hand ends of lines survive on this strip.

IMPORTANT ORIENTATION NOTE: on this face the script is upside down in the photographs (the pencil shelfmarks are written the other way up from the medieval text). I read from 180-degree-rotated crops. Line numbers below are counted from the top of the ROTATED crop (= reading order), which is the BOTTOM of the original image upward. In reading orientation the surviving text is the LEFT edge of a column (initials and paragraph marks at line starts, left margin with small marginal notes and reference letters); line ends are cut away on the right. So on this face each line gives only the first c. 6-12 letters.
(Correction to my image-002 note: the "right-hand ends" remark there was made before I noticed the inversion; it is line beginnings that survive.)

==================== SUMMARY / LIMITATIONS ====================
- Selected spans: all text on face image-001 (both strips, every tile), which preserves the first c. 6-12 letters of each line of one textura column with its left margin (marginal reference letters a, b, c, d, e, f keying paragraph marks; "Nota" monograms; small faint glosses). Face image-010 preserves the corresponding line ends and right margin, but is heavily abraded; there I could read only isolated line endings, plus three LATER CURSIVE additions (image-012 block of c. 23 lines; image-013 note of 6 lines; image-015 note of 4 lines), read only in part.
- Face image-001 text is upside down in the photographs; I worked from 180-degree rotations. Reading order: left strip = 008 -> 006 -> 004 (-> blank 002); right strip = 009 (framed block in larger script, with rubric line and display letters) -> 007 -> 005 -> 003.
- Observations, not interpretations: frequent allegation-style abbreviations "l.", "ff.", "c.", "ii.", "ex(tra)?", "arg(umentum)?", "in fine"; legal-sounding vocabulary (pacta, uenditor, dolo, iudex, post s(e)n(tent)iam, instru(men)ta, electio(n)e, iudicis, legato, testib(us), obligat-, p(ro)curat-, episcopis, doctorib(us)). On right strip a framed larger-script section with a rubric "l. ?(s)eparatioi/Exp?atioi . Nou[...]", decorative display letters, and text including "C Hac igit(ur)", "Sciat-", "doctorib(us) & aliis ep(iscop)is(?)", "ueteru(m)".
- Every reading here is uncertain at the letter level; only line beginnings survive, so no line is complete. Overlaps between vertically adjacent tiles were matched and not counted twice. No work or author identified.
- Not done / suggestions: face image-010 might yield more under UV or multispectral imaging; a wider view of the original binding position is not needed for reading. No areas were deliberately skipped.
- Process note: beyond the brief I made rotated and contrast-enhanced crops (all under responses-rerun/crops/packet-18/). I did not stop on the image limit.
